summary: A short memo from the Network Working Group chair urging sites to set real schedules for finishing their software. Each site's liaison was asked to give dates for implementing the Host-Host protocol as changed by RFC 107, plus Telnet programs for users and servers. John Heafner at Rand agreed to track progress and test implementations.

subtitle: The Network Working Group chair asks every site for a real schedule for its network software.

tldr.problem: It was time to set serious schedules for implementing NCPs and Telnets at the sites on the network.
tldr.mechanism: Each site's Network Liaison Contact must prepare a schedule with dates for seven milestones and send it to John Heafner of Rand, who monitors progress and tests implementations.
tldr.outcome: John also becomes the person to complain to about ambiguities, insufficiencies and misunderstandings of the protocols. The RFC was updated by RFC 130.

sections.title: The Request for Schedules
sections.content:
This short memo from Steve Crocker says it is time to set serious schedules for the implementation of NCPs (Network Control Programs) and Telnets. To help, John Heafner of Rand agreed to monitor each site's progress and test its implementation.

Network Liaison Contacts are made responsible for preparing a schedule and informing John. The memo is marked as updating RFC 107.
sections.plainLanguage: The class leader says it is time to pick finish dates. A helper named John will keep track.

sections.title: What a Schedule Must Cover
sections.content:
A schedule must include dates for implementing an NCP according to the specifications in Document #1 as modified by RFC 107, a user-Telnet that lets local users log in to foreign Hosts, and a server-Telnet that lets foreign users log in on your Host.

It must also give dates for documenting how to connect and log in to your Host, documenting how to obtain job numbers and passwords, documenting the services available on your Host, and reaching regular operation at advertised hours.
sections.plainLanguage: Each school must say when its mailbox will work, when visitors can come in, and when it will write down the rules for visiting.

sections.title: John Heafner's Role
sections.content:
John is responsible for prodding Host teams to produce the schedule, software and documentation, for testing the advertised implementations, and for probing and understanding the reasons for unseemly delays.

The memo adds that John is now the right person to complain to about ambiguities, insufficiencies and misunderstandings of the protocols.
sections.plainLanguage: John nudges people who are late, checks that things work, and listens when something in the rules is confusing.

references.text: RFC 107, referenced as modifying the specifications in Document #1.
